newsitem.title: EGYPT: EMU important but not crucial - SBC economist.
newsitem.headline: EMU important but not crucial - SBC economist.

text.p: European economic and monetary union is important to currency markets but not crucial because Europe is already integrating and adjusting to face world competition, the head of economic research for Swiss Bank Corp in London, Marc Hendriks, said on Friday.
"The euro is important but it is a bit of a sideshow," he told the annual congress of the InterArab Cambist Association.
"The days of asking if (EMU) will happen are past. There now seems a fighting chance we will end with a "Big Bang' of monetary union, with all reasonable contenders permitted to participate."
European capital markets are already integrating, spreads are narrowing and there will be much freer capital flows between countries.
"That is the sea change in Europe, in which the euro has a role to play. But it is not the catalyst," he said.
The euro will remove the choice of diversification in currencies but there will be much wider choice of assets which will instead provide diversification.
Europeans will no longer rest content with buying government paper and a common currency will ease cross-border comparisons of equity investment, he said.
It is likely that European currency bond markets will continue to converge to give a spread of only 50 to 100 basis points.
European central banks have already moved from targeting monetary variables to targeting exchange rates.

"Currencies under strong upward pressure have seen strong monetary growth," he said. "That means the outlook for European interest rates is no change as far as I can see. The risk is that interest rates may fall."
